Tavern
======

(Redirected from [Emporium](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/index.php?title=Emporium&redirect=no "Emporium")
)

[![War Table.png](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/images/9/9d/War_Table.png)](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/File:War_Table.png)

There are currently 2 Different Hubs in the game, the Private Tavern and the Heroes Market Place also known as the Town.  
This is where you'll spend any time not in battle to sell, buy, manage, tinker and test any gear you've found in combat.  
  

The Tavern and Town also has multiple [NPCs](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Non_Playable_Characters "Non Playable Characters")
 with various shops, services and fun interactions.  
  
  

### 

The War Table

The War Table is the means by which players can start and join games in Dungeon Defenders 2. The war table is directly in front of the player when they enter the town or tavern. Interacting with the War Table brings up the World Map, which allows players to select maps based on which gamemode and difficulty they want. Players can also click the Advanced tab in the top right to have more options, selecting maps, regions, difficulty, mode and creating a game with a name and requirements to join.  
You can also browse for other people's open games here.  

### 

The Emporium

The Emporium consists of 4 [Vendors](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Non_Playable_Characters "Non Playable Characters")
 that sell costumes for you, your towers, and even has weapons with on-kill animations.  
The Emporium is furthermore filled with different [Costumes](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Costumes "Costumes")
 and [Tower Skins](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Tower_Skins "Tower Skins")
.

### 

The Training Dummies

These fine indestructible dummies will show you how much damage a tower, or hero, does with its attacks.  
The smaller dummies show a general DPS in yellow text every few seconds.  
The bigger dummies will show the total amount of damage done to them, how much time it took and the corresponding DPS.  
Each big dummy has a name, these names refer to developers, closed beta testers and influencers of the game.  

**Damage Numbers Colors:**  

*   White = Physical Damage  
    
*   Pink = Magical Damage  
    
*   Red = Critical Hits  
    
*   Grey = Self Inflicted Damage  
    
*   Dark Purple = Storm Damage  
    
*   Very Dark Purple = Oil Damage  
    
*   Light Blue = Ice Damage
